sections.title: Git Version Control
sections.description: Branching, merging, rebasing, and repository management.

questions.prompt: Which command creates a new Git branch named "feature" and immediately switches to it?
questions.explanation: git checkout -b feature creates and checks out the new branch in one command.

questions.prompt: What is the primary difference between `git merge` and `git rebase`?
questions.explanation: Rebase rewrites project history by moving commits onto a new base, creating a linear history.

options.text: git merge deletes history, git rebase preserves it
git rebase rewrites commit history to create a linear sequence
git merge is only used for remote repositories
There is no difference; they are exact aliases

questions.prompt: Which command allows you to temporarily shelve (store) uncommitted changes without committing them?
questions.explanation: git stash saves uncommitted modifications to a temporary stack.

questions.prompt: How do you discard changes in a working directory file `app.js` and restore it to the LAST commit?
questions.explanation: git checkout -- app.js or git restore app.js discards local changes.

questions.prompt: Which Git command shows the commit hash, author, date, and commit message history?
questions.explanation: git log outputs commit history details.

sections.title: Linux Systems Administration
sections.description: CLI commands, file permissions, processes, and networking.

questions.prompt: Which numeric permission code corresponds to `rwxr-xr--` in Linux chmod syntax?
Which command searches for the pattern "ERROR" across all `.log` files recursively in `/var/log`?
questions.explanation: grep -rn "ERROR" /var/log/*.log performs recursive pattern matching with line numbers.

questions.prompt: What tool is used to monitor real-time system process metrics, CPU, and memory consumption in terminal?
questions.explanation: htop / top gives real-time process statistics.

questions.prompt: Which command checks active listening TCP ports and associated processes in Linux?
questions.explanation: ss -tulpn or netstat -tulpn lists listening ports and PIDs.

questions.prompt: How do you send a background SIGTERM signal to terminate a process with PID 4321?
questions.explanation: kill 4321 sends default SIGTERM (15) to PID 4321.

sections.title: Docker & CI/CD Pipelines
sections.description: Containerization, Dockerfile optimizations, and automated build flows.

questions.prompt: Which Dockerfile instruction specifies the default command executed when a container starts?
questions.explanation: CMD specifies the execution defaults for a starting container.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of multi-stage Docker builds?
questions.explanation: Multi-stage builds allow separating build tools from final production images to keep image size minimal.

options.text: To produce smaller production images by discarding build-time tools
To compile code without installing Docker engine

questions.prompt: Which command removes all stopped containers, unused networks, and dangling images in Docker?
questions.explanation: docker system prune cleans up unused Docker resources.

questions.prompt: In Docker Compose, which keyword links host directory `./data` to container path `/app/data`?
questions.explanation: volumes mounts host paths into containers.

questions.prompt: Select all features that characterize immutable infrastructure deployment:
questions.explanation: Immutable infrastructure replaces servers entirely rather than modifying them in place.

options.text: Servers are never modified after creation; they are replaced
Requires SSH into live production servers to apply hotfixes
Uses versioned images/templates for automated rollbacks
